note: Inputs only. Rate constants of the authors' second (modified) first-order model for pulsed-potential electrolysis on Cu60Zn40, fitted by the Simplex/linear-programming procedure of the appendix. Tables 7.26 and 7.27 hold removal/selectivity results (AC mains feed; other electrodes), not rate constants, and were not transcribed.

files.extracted.csv: tidy long: one row per constant (k_j and its time-weighted value)

csv_columns.reaction: step assigned to k_j in scheme 7.18 and eqs 39-42 (printed pp. 173-174)
csv_columns.half_cycle: reduction constants act during the negative potential (time t1), oxidation constants during the positive potential (t2) (printed p. 173)
csv_columns.time_fraction_label_printed: t_i in the printed (t_i/T) column, read from the flattened text layer
csv_columns.time_fraction_expected: t_i/T implied by the half cycle: t1/T = 0.8 (cathodic -1.5 V, 80 %), t2/T = 0.2 (anodic +1.5 V, 20 %)
csv_columns.flag: 'uncertain' where the time weighting is inconsistent

provenance.citation: Polatides C., Electrochemical removal of nitrate from aqueous solutions and environmental samples using constant and pulsed potential, PhD thesis (in Greek), Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, Dept. of Chemical Engineering (2007); supervisor G. Kyriacou

model_translated.scheme_7p18: NO3- <-> NO2- (k1 forward, k-1 back), NO2- -> NH3 (k2), NH3 -> N2 (k3), NO2- -> N2 (k4), NH3 -> NO3- (k5), NO3- -> N2 (k6); k1, k2, k4, k6 are reductions during the negative potential, k-1, k3, k5 oxidations during the positive potential; all first order (printed pp. 173-174).
model_translated.eqs_39_42: -d[NO3-]/dt = (t1/T)k1[NO3-] - (t2/T)k-1[NO2-] - (t2/T)k5[NH3] + (t1/T)k6[NO3-]; d[NO2-]/dt = (t1/T)k1[NO3-] - (t2/T)k-1[NO2-] - (t1/T)k4[NO2-] - (t1/T)k2[NO2-]; d[NH3]/dt = (t1/T)k2[NO2-] - (t2/T)k3[NH3] - (t2/T)k5[NH3]; d[N2]/dt = (t1/T)k6[NO3-] + (t1/T)k4[NO2-] + (t2/T)k3[NH3] (reconstructed from the flattened text layer; the N2 equation has no factor 1/2, so N2 is on an N-atom basis if N is conserved).
model_translated.fit_target: Diag 7.8 data (asymmetric square pulse 80 %-20 %, 50 Hz, the run with the highest gaseous selectivity) (printed p. 172)
model_translated.fit_method: Adams-Bashforth-Moulton integration failed for both models; the Simplex/linear-programming route (4th-degree polynomial fits, derivatives at sampling times, Excel Solver; appendix printed pp. 196-197) gave satisfactory results only for model 2 (printed p. 174). N2 fit mean absolute error 7 % (printed p. 177).
model_translated.text_printed_p178: 'The reduction reaction of nitrites [sic, nitrates] to nitrites was found to have k1 = 0.003343 min-1 and is slower than the reduction of nitrites to ammonia, k2 = 0.075 min-1. N2 is produced faster by ammonia oxidation, k3 = 0.02865 min-1, than by nitrite reduction, k4 = 0.003522 min-1, while direct reduction of nitrate to nitrogen is the slowest, k6 = 0.000353 min-1.'

conditions.waveform: asymmetric square pulse, 50 Hz, cathodic -1.5 V vs Ag/AgCl for 80 % of the period, anodic +1.5 V for 20 %
conditions.electrolyte: not restated for Diag 7.8; the chapter-7 Cu60Zn40 experiments use 0.1 M K2SO4 + 0.05 M KNO3 (Table 7.5 caption) - inferred

checks.result: Six of seven ratios equal the expected t_i/T (0.8 for reductions, 0.2 for oxidations) to <0.1 %. k2 (NO2- -> NH3, a reduction) has 0.015/0.075 = 0.2, the oxidation weight.
checks.pulse_naming: Printed p. 155-156 defines an '80 %-20 %' pulse as one with 80 % of the period at the positive potential and 20 % at the cathodic potential, and Diag 7.2 is captioned '20 %-80 %', while every experiment caption uses 'cathodic -1.5 V (80 %), anodic +1.5 V (20 %)'. The values here follow the experiment captions (t1/T = 0.8 cathodic).

transcription_method: thesis text layer: per-page text layer of the National Archive of PhD Theses online reader (EKT freader), read and typed in by an agent on 2026-10-20; table layout reconstructed by hand from the flattened text; every row's printed number sequence was checked by script to occur verbatim on the cited page (literature/extraction_scripts/thesis_tables/build_tables.py). Page images of these pages were not viewed. Not yet re-checked by a person.
